skill.name: robots-sitemap-validator
skill.description: Validate local robots.txt and sitemap XML files for crawl blockers, malformed directives, invalid URLs, and common size limits.
skill.summary: Find crawl configuration mistakes before deployment.
skill.author: justhandledlabs

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns across four files. Semantic review found no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, destructive behavior, or business-logic abuse.

content.value_statement: Crawl configuration mistakes can hide pages from search engines or produce invalid sitemap data. This skill checks local robots.txt and sitemap XML files and reports actionable findings.
actual_capabilities: Detects robots.txt directives that block the entire site.
Flags malformed and unknown robots.txt directives.
Reports missing Sitemap directives and absent sibling sitemap files.
Parses sitemap XML and reports malformed documents.
Checks sitemap locations for absolute URLs and mixed HTTP schemes.
Flags sitemaps exceeding common URL count or uncompressed size guidance.
limitations: Reads local files or standard input only and cannot inspect a deployed site.
Does not fetch URLs, test HTTP responses, or submit sitemaps.
Does not modify robots.txt or sitemap files.
The sibling check assumes the referenced sitemap basename is beside robots.txt.

use_cases.title: Prelaunch Crawl Review
use_cases.description: Check deployment files for blockers and malformed sitemap data before a site launch.

use_cases.title: Build Pipeline Validation
use_cases.description: Scan generated crawl files and surface findings before a release proceeds.

use_cases.title: Indexing Issue Triage
use_cases.description: Review local crawl configuration when important pages appear absent from search results.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [folder] for robots.txt and sitemap.xml issues. Summarize each finding with severity, file, line, and a plain remediation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear local crawlability check.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Specific Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate [robots.txt path] and [sitemap.xml path]. Separate crawl blockers from lower-priority quality warnings.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants focused results for known files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Build Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan [build directory] and compare results with [expected rules]. Highlight missing files, malformed XML, and absolute URL problems.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is checking generated files before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [directory] for release readiness. Prioritize high-severity findings, explain likely crawler impact, and propose a verification checklist without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a structured crawl configuration review.

output_examples.input: Check the deployment folder for crawl blockers.
output: High: robots.txt blocks the entire site with a root disallow rule.
Medium: robots.txt has no Sitemap directive.

output_examples.input: Validate the local robots.txt and sitemap.xml files.
output_examples.output: Two files were scanned. No supported validation issues were found.

output_examples.input: Review the generated sitemap before release.
output: High: The sitemap XML is not well formed.
Fix the reported XML location, regenerate the sitemap, and scan it again.

best_practices: Scan the exact files produced by the deployment build.
Review intentional private-area rules before removing any disallow directive.
Run the validator again after every crawl configuration change.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a clean local scan as proof that the live site is crawlable.
Do not remove intentional access restrictions without confirming site requirements.
Do not assume an absent sibling sitemap proves the production sitemap is unavailable.

faq.question: Does this skill access my live website?
faq.answer: No. It reads local files or standard input and makes no network requests.

faq.question: Which files can it validate?
faq.answer: It validates robots.txt files and files whose names begin with sitemap and end with .xml.

faq.question: Will it repair my files?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and remediation guidance without changing files.

faq.question: What does an absent sibling sitemap finding mean?
faq.answer: The referenced sitemap basename was not beside robots.txt locally. The production URL may still resolve, so review the deployment output.

faq.question: Does a clean report guarantee search indexing?
faq.answer: No. The validator cannot confirm deployment, HTTP responses, authentication, page quality, or search engine decisions.

faq.question: Can I use it in a build pipeline?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python script accepts paths and can produce Markdown or JSON output for downstream checks.
